text:
1. The ocean covers about 71% of Earth's surface.
2. The ocean holds about 97% of Earth's water.
3. The Pacific is the largest ocean and covers more area than all of Earth's land combined.
4. The Arctic is the smallest and shallowest of the five oceans.
5. The average ocean depth is about 3,700 meters.
6. The deepest known point, Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench, is about 11,000 meters down.
7. About a quarter of the seafloor has been mapped in high resolution.
8. Seawater is about 3.5% salt on average.
9. Salt lowers the freezing point of seawater to about -2°C.
10. Seawater is denser than fresh water, at roughly 1,025 kg per cubic meter.
11. Sound travels about 4.3 times faster in seawater than in air.
12. The ocean absorbs roughly 90% of the extra heat trapped by greenhouse gases.
13. The ocean absorbs about a quarter of the carbon dioxide humans emit.
14. Phytoplankton, microscopic ocean algae, produce a large share of the oxygen on Earth.
15. Sunlight fades out at about 1,000 meters, below which lies the midnight zone.
16. Most deep-sea animals can produce their own light, a trait called bioluminescence.
17. Most of the ocean remains unexplored.
18. Tides are caused mainly by the Moon's gravity.
19. Most ocean waves are generated by wind.
20. Rogue waves can exceed 25 meters in height.
21. Tsunamis can travel across deep ocean at jet-airliner speeds, up to about 800 km/h.
22. The Gulf Stream carries warm water that moderates the climate of northwestern Europe.
23. Global ocean circulation, driven by temperature and salinity, takes roughly 1,000 years to complete one loop.
24. The Mid-Atlantic Ridge spreads apart by roughly 2.5 cm per year, slowly widening the Atlantic.
25. Coral reefs cover less than 1% of the seafloor but support about a quarter of known marine species.
26. Hydrothermal vents support ecosystems that run on chemical energy rather than sunlight.
27. Blue whales are the largest animals known to have lived, reaching about 30 meters long.
28. The giant squid has the largest eyes of any animal, about 27 cm across.
29. Sperm whales can dive deeper than 2,000 meters to hunt giant squid.
30. Emperor penguins can dive more than 500 meters.
31. Octopuses have three hearts.
32. Sea otters use rocks as tools to crack open shellfish.
33. Humpback whales sing long, complex songs that change over time.
34. The immortal jellyfish, Turritopsis dohrnii, can revert to its juvenile stage when injured or stressed.
35. Plastic debris has been found across the ocean, from the surface to the deepest trenches.
36. The first crewed descent to Challenger Deep was in 1960.
37. The ocean supplies much of the protein eaten by people worldwide.
38. Marine life exists at every depth, including the deepest trenches.
39. Ocean water temperature varies widely, from below freezing near the poles to over 30°C in tropical shallows.
40. Some marine organisms have evolved to survive crushing pressures of over 1,000 times sea-level air pressure in the deep.
